chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abdullah ibn al-Mustanir from al-Munjaliq ibn Umar said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, for the Master of this Matter there are two occultations; one of them is long, until some say: He has died! And some say: He has been killed! And some say: He has gone! Until only a few of his companions remain upon his matter. None of his offspring or others will be informed of his location, except the Servant who manages his affairs.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Matter (Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of Imam Mahdi and how does the first one affect his companions?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological significance of the Major Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Kubra*), where the prolonged absence of Imam al-Mahdi tests the faith of his followers through widespread speculation about his death or disappearance. It underscores the concept of *al-Mawla al-Mu'tamad* (the trusted deputy), who serves as the exclusive link to the Imam during this period, preserving the continuity of divine authority despite the hidden nature of his physical presence.
